::api-operation{method="GET" path="/v1/countries/{code}/subdivisions"}
#docs
## Path parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | `string` | **yes** | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, case-insensitive |

## Response

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `object` | `string` | The object type; always `list`. One of `list`. |
| `data` | `array of object` | The rows on this page. |
| `data.object` | `string` | The object type; always `subdivision`. One of `subdivision`. |
| `data.code` | `string` | The ISO 3166-2 SUFFIX ("TN", not "IN-TN") — what an address `state_code` stores. |
| `data.name` | `string` | The state or region's name. |
| `aliases` | `object` | Non-canonical codes we also accept, as { alias: canonical }. A picker needs them to render an imported value (OD) against our canonical code (OR); without the fold the field shows blank for a correct value and the next save silently clears it. |
| `region_label` | `string` | Repeated here so a control that knows only the country code can label itself without also fetching /v1/countries. |
| `subdivision_strict` | `boolean` | True if the country's subdivision list is complete and addresses must use it. |

## Status codes

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Success |
| `404` | No such country |

#request
```bash [Request]
curl "$TMBILLING_URL/v1/countries/US/subdivisions"
```

#response

```json [200 OK]
      "object": "subdivision",
      "code": "TN",
      "name": "Tamil Nadu"
    }
  ],
  "aliases": {},
  "region_label": "State",
  "subdivision_strict": false
}
```
